R7AF-bear-walk-0003.name: By Durney Creek
R7AF-bear-walk-0003.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R7AF-bear-walk-0003.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2010 (16 years old), 90 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2016 (fire G70057), 480 m E: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
Durney Creek 20 m NE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Tumbler Ridge, about 94 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 55.61802, -121.43845, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 380 m NW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 8 m, about 8 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-21, Region 7B. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
R7AF-bear-walk-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 7-21: about 704 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.10 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.4 km and about 8 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
